name: Chinese nationalism
summary: Chinese nationalism holds that the Chinese people form one nation whose unity, sovereignty and territory must be defended and whose standing must be restored after a century of foreign humiliation. Founded in Sun Yat-sen's nationalism and Chiang Kai-shek's China's Destiny, its current state form is the 'great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation' and the demand for complete reunification with Taiwan. It is anti-imperialist, treats the nation's culture and unity as inherited from antiquity, and rejects secession.
scope: The nationalist core only: Sun Yat-sen's principle of nationalism (as expounded by Linebarger), Chiang Kai-shek's China's Destiny, and the state's nationalist texts on sovereignty and Taiwan (Anti-Secession Law, 2022 white paper, Xi's 2014 rejuvenation speech). It leaves out the Communist Party's and the Kuomintang's wider economic and political programmes, Deng-era reform doctrine, and Taiwanese Chinese identity politics, which are not positions of the nationalism itself.

notes: Searched all themes in Chiang's China's Destiny, Linebarger's Sun, the Taiwan white paper, Anti-Secession Law, Xi's 2014 speech and the 20th Congress report. Chinese nationalism's own texts speak to territory, sovereignty, the nation's unity and culture, anti-imperialism and the use of force over Taiwan; economics, social policy, ecology, technology and most civil-liberty and government-structure questions belong to the Party or the Kuomintang rather than to the nationalism, so they are null. Kuomintang and PRC strands differ on minorities (assimilation versus regional autonomy). Government, liberty and economy themes are thin by design. Sources blocked: Zhao Suisheng, Unger and Duara (lending-library or paywalled copies), Leibold and Jenco open-access PDFs (403).
